title: Agentic Game Development as a Verifiable Trajectory Data Engine for Scaling World Models
task: Scaling world models via game-engine reward signals for spatial generation
key_results: RLHEV combines dense engine physics/collision signals with human feedback; enables RL post-training for video world models via executable game specifications
comments: Clever insight that game engines provide verifiable rewards analogous to compilers for code agents, addressing the fuzzy-signal problem in spatial generation.

model_io.model: World model (spatial generation) + game engine verifier

hypotheses.hypothesis: Game development provides grounded reward signals superior to CLIP-based proxies for spatial world-model RL post-training
hypotheses.result: Engine verification enables dense rewards; proposed RLHEV paradigm combines engine signals with human feedback

title: PAWBench: How Far Are We from Probabilistically Aligned World Modeling?
task: Evaluating whether video generators match ground-truth distributions of physical behaviors
key_results: No model consistently matches reference probabilities across 50 scenarios and 11 systems; gap remains between current video generators and probabilistically aligned world modeling
comments: PAWBench formally defines a critical gap: plausibility ≠ distributional correctness, exposing a fundamental evaluation blind spot in current video generation literature.

inputs: repeated video rollouts from 11 video generation systems

hypotheses.hypothesis: Current video generators achieve individual-video plausibility but fail probabilistic alignment across repeated rollouts
hypotheses.result: No model consistently recovers correct distribution of valid behaviors; 50 scenarios show systematic distributional mismatch

title: UrbanGround: From Local Perception to Spatial Agency in a Real-Scale City
task: Testing multimodal LLM agents' grounding and navigation in realistic urban environments
key_results: MLLM agents show atomic visual recognition and short-range reasoning but fail sustained goal-directed behavior; errors accumulate over extended exploration in Hong Kong 3D replica
comments: UrbanGround exposes a critical failure mode: local perceptual abilities do not compose into reliable long-horizon behavior, reflecting real deployment challenges.

model_io.model: MLLM agent with first-person perception + interactive map

hypotheses.hypothesis: MLLM agents can ground local scenes and answer spatial questions after active observation
hypotheses.result: Agents show useful visual recognition but grounding degrades; navigation reliability fails at extended distances

hypotheses.hypothesis: Short-range spatial abilities compose into sustained navigation as destinations vary in distance and explicitness
hypotheses.result: Composition fails; orientation and pedestrian-aware movement remain unreliable; error correction is ineffective

title: TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization
task: Test-time mathematical reasoning without ground-truth labels via policy optimization
key_results: TTPO matches label-supervised OPSD on five benchmarks; raises Qwen3-1.7B from 38.0% to 45.2% in test-time training; +25.2%–+36.4% improvement without reasoning chains
comments: Asymmetric objective elegantly handles label-noise by learning differently from agreeing vs. disagreeing rollouts; a clever self-supervised reasoning approach.

model_io.model: LLM with TTPO (asymmetric OPSD + Grouped RL + token-level selection)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Majority-vote pseudo-labels corrupt teachers and mislead tokens but this failure is asymmetric: disagreeing rollouts are typically wrong regardless of vote correctness
hypotheses.result: TTPO exploits asymmetry via separate distillation (agreeing) and RL (disagreeing) branches; matches supervised OPSD without labels

title: Self-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Flow Matching Models without Teacher
task: Teacher-free on-policy distillation for flow matching via self-exploration
key_results: Self-OPD outperforms RL and OPD methods without task-specific teachers on single and mixed reward benchmarks; branches K stochastic SDE candidates and compares rewards
comments: Avoids expensive teacher training by using the student's own exploration; direction-aware attenuation and reward-level fusion elegantly handle multi-objective conflicts.

model_io.model: Flow matching model with Self-OPD (K-branch stochastic SDE exploration)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Student self-exploration can replace task-specific teacher models and reduce distribution discrepancy in OPD
hypotheses.result: Self-OPD branches student predictions, compares rewards against baseline, pulls high-advantage and repels low-advantage branches without external teacher

title: What Makes Good Agentic Data? An ACE Lens on Data Generation for LLM Agents
task: Unified framework for agentic data generation spanning environment, task, interaction, and verification
key_results: ACE lens organizes generation paradigms (Accuracy: feasible support, Complexity: learner-relative, divErsity: coverage); shift toward execution-grounded accuracy and learner-adaptive complexity
comments: Factorized representation (E,q,τ,v) provides conceptual clarity but the paper is primarily a survey/framework rather than introducing new methods.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Agentic data quality depends on consistency among environment, task, interaction, and verification signals rather than volume alone
hypotheses.result: ACE framework shows literature shift toward execution-grounded accuracy, learner-relative complexity calibration, and diversity beyond surface variation

comments: Eliminates on-chip phase shifters via coherent digital processing, but scalability to higher element counts and real-time processing throughput require further assessment.

model_io.model: 128-element photonic integrated circuit optical phased array at 1550 nm
inputs: local oscillator at 1550 nm distributed to 128 receivers

hypotheses.hypothesis: Fully parallelized coherent detection enables effective digital beamforming without on-chip phase shifters
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 6-element subset achieves 1.23° beamwidth and 8.30° field-of-view with sub-degree phase noise

title: Biomimetic design and optimization of aero-engine blades inspired by humpback whale tubercles
task: Aero-engine blade optimization via humpback whale tubercle biomimicry
key_results: Single-channel flow rate increased 4.09%; pressure ratio increased 4.85%; blade efficiency improved from 67.014% to 89.861%; maximum deformation reduced from 0.306% to 0.239%
comments: Bionic tubercle design suppresses flow separation and enhances aerodynamic efficiency, but structural stiffness and fatigue performance under high-speed cyclic loading require optimization before engine deployment.

model_io.model: Turbine fan blade with humpback whale tubercle biomimetic airfoil

hypotheses.hypothesis: Tubercle-induced flow control suppresses vortex dissipation and improves fan blade efficiency
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: bionic blade achieves 4.85% pressure ratio increase and 22.8 percentage point efficiency gain; structural strength slightly enhanced

title: Four faces of information in natural systems
task: Conceptual disambiguation of 'information' across scientific disciplines
key_results: Four distinct technical interpretations identified: engineering, statistical, thermodynamic, and ontological 'faces' of information; pluralistic framework proposed
comments: Perspective articulates conceptual fragmentation in information science, but lacks quantitative metrics or algorithmic reconciliation between competing definitions.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multiple coexisting technical interpretations of 'information' serve distinct scientific domains with complementary affordances
hypotheses.result: Supported through literature survey across physics, computer science, and natural systems; monolithic approach deemed insufficient
